text:
incident-bot: Pager: REDWOOD-INFER-EU latency SLO breach in eu-west-1 — 95th p95 > 800ms over 3m. Alert: 3 consecutive windows
Olivia: I’m on it. seeing spikes for text-gen and embeddings.
Raj: thundering herd? any deploys recently?
Olivia: no deploys past 2h. infra looks healthy but individual serving hosts show high GPU utilization.
Sam: @Olivia can you paste the top hosts?
Olivia: sure — top 3 GPU hosts by load: gpu-eu-12 (98%), gpu-eu-11 (95%), gpu-eu-08 (87%)
Maria: Are we seeing traffic shift from us-east? Any cross-region failover kicking in?
Olivia: Checking. Traffic origin shows steady europe-origin traffic, but a surge from a partner customer (id: partner-omega) — roughly +220% P50 qps.
Kevin: can we throttle that customer or route to dedicated pool?
Raj: we have a routing policy in console — can force partner traffic to fallback model-small or route to dedicated if available.
Olivia: For now I added a temporary rule to route partner-omega to model-small (lower memory config) to shed some load, and enabled prefix caching for embeddings for that key.
incident-bot: Action logged: temporary routing rule applied by Olivia — change-id: ch_2026_1860001123
Sam: good. Did p95 drop after the change?
Olivia: p95 dropped from ~860ms -> ~420ms within 90s. errors are stable.
Maria: customer facing? any 5xx spikes?
Olivia: no 5xx increase. only latency. Verified no SLO burn for embeddings pipeline for customers except partner-omega which had degraded latency.
Raj: OK we need to avoid noisy alerts during the mitigation and postmortem. The eu latency alert fired repeatedly — we should add a suppression window for the ongoing incident and add an alert noise policy.
Sam: I’ll take over handoff in 10m — Olivia, document current mitigation steps and post a quick runbook note.
Olivia: posted runbook snippet to the incident doc channel: "force-route partner-omega -> model-small; enable prefix KV cache; scale up gpu-eu-13 (if capacity)"
Kevin: Trying a quick scale: kubectl -n redwood scale statefulset/gpu-serving-eu --replicas=4
Kevin: pods coming up, but warmup takes ~60s due to model load.
Raj: can we create a temporary alert rule: if a single customer exceeds 150% of normal rate and causes p95 spike, trigger customer-throttle task instead of full-region pager?
Maria: yes we should add a metric for per-customer qps and a composite alert that routes to a tiered notification.
Sam: Oncall handoff: I’m now primary for this incident — @Olivia please ping if anything escalates.
Olivia: pinged. I’ll stay nearby for a bit.
incident-bot: Handoff logged: previous_oncall=Olivia new_oncall=Sam at 1860001400
Sam: Observability notes for post-incident: 1) reduce eu latency alert sensitivity: change window from 3m to 5m and require 2 consecutive evaluation periods; 2) add per-customer rate anomaly alert; 3) build a multi-region dashboard tile to show regional p95, active sessions by origin, and queued requests.
Raj: also disable the old alert that fires on any p95 > 400ms for the entire org — it was too noisy. We'll create a scoped alert: region + model-class + customer-tier.
Maria: We should also author a failover monitor: synthetic requests from us-east, eu-west, ap-south hitting /health and /v1/generate, and an automated sanity check that if eu p95 > 750ms for 6m then route non-enterprise traffic to us-east.
Kevin: I can add the synthetic checks in Datadog: "multi-region-health" monitors for each endpoint, with a composite monitor that compares regions.
Olivia: sample log snippet for the spike (truncated):
```
[2026-03-11T14:02:12Z] request_id=abc123 src=partner-omega model=text-gen size=2048 latency_ms=1200 host=gpu-eu-12
[2026-03-11T14:02:13Z] request_id=abc124 src=partner-omega model=embeddings size=512 latency_ms=980 host=gpu-eu-11
```
Sam: Nice. For the postmortem and action items, we should: 
- adjust alert thresholds and add suppression rules during mitigations
- create per-customer qps anomaly alerts
- add multi-region synthetic health monitors + failover runbook
- add a dashboard with traffic-by-origin and model-class p95 breakdown
- update runbook to include 'temporary routing to model-small' step
Olivia: I'll open the incident ticker and assign tasks.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0311-042 — link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0311-042
Raj: Quick note on alert tuning specifics: change eu p95 alert to query: max(last_5m(p95)) > 700ms AND count_over_time(queries by region and customer) > baseline*1.3; set notification to pager only if impacted_customers > 5. Otherwise, post to eng-sre.
Sam: Agree. Also, create a dashboard widget that shows: region p95, per-customer top 10 traffic, GPU utilization by host.
Maria: After action: schedule a 30m run with partners to discuss client-side rate limits or batching for partner-omega.
Kevin: I'll submit the Datadog monitor updates and the synthetic checks by EOD.
Olivia: closing the active mitigation: partner throttled and route change reverted to normal for stable traffic. Will keep the new monitors in place.
Sam: Marking incident as under control. Will follow up with a short postmortem doc and the alert tuning PR.
incident-bot: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigated at 1860004300
Olivia: Thanks team :thumbsup:
Raj: assigning follow-ups: @Kevin update monitors, @Maria schedule partner sync, @Olivia draft postmortem, @Sam PR for alert-changes.
Sam: I’ll draft the alert PR with the new thresholds and suppression windows.
Olivia: leaving a final note in the incident doc about failover thresholds and sample queries.
Sam: Great. I’ll take responsibility for closing once PR merged and monitors in prod.
Kevin: will post monitor IDs here when done.
Maria: thanks all.
